set_title: Chest and airway signs: Hamman crunch, Hoover sign, Platypnea-orthodeoxia, Oliver sign (tracheal tug) and Pemberton sign
stem: A 45-year-old man develops severe chest pain after forceful vomiting following a binge. A crackling, clicking sound synchronous with his heartbeat is heard over the precordium, and crepitus is felt at the base of the neck.
oneliner: 45M, severe chest pain after forceful vomiting + crackling sound with each heartbeat → ?

whyNot.A: Hoover sign is inward rib movement in COPD; his finding is a **heartbeat-synchronous crackle**
whyNot.B: Platypnea-orthodeoxia is upright desaturation; his finding is a **crackle with each heartbeat**
whyNot.D: Oliver sign is a tracheal tug; his finding is a **precordial crackle after vomiting**
whyNot.E: Pemberton sign is facial flushing on raising the arms; his is a **heartbeat-synchronous crackle**

why: Hamman crunch is a crunching sound synchronous with the heartbeat from air in the mediastinum. **Forceful vomiting with neck crepitus** suggests esophageal rupture (Boerhaave).

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Lower ribs pull inward on inspiration
Dyspnea and hypoxia when upright, better lying
Trachea tugs downward with each heartbeat
Face flushes when both arms are raised
Substernal goiter obstructing the thoracic inlet

idea.rule: Heartbeat-synchronous crunch after vomiting = pneumomediastinum, Boerhaave.
also: Rupture is usually at the distal left esophagus

set_title: Chest and airway signs: Hamman crunch, Hoover sign, Platypnea-orthodeoxia, Oliver sign (tracheal tug) and Pemberton sign
stem: A 58-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis has dyspnea. His oxygen saturation is 97% lying flat and falls to 86% when he sits upright. Spider angiomata are present.
oneliner: 58M, cirrhosis, dyspnea + SpO2 97% supine, 86% upright → ?

whyNot.A: Hamman crunch is a heartbeat-synchronous sound; his finding is **desaturation when upright**
whyNot.B: Hoover sign is inward rib movement in COPD; his finding is **desaturation when upright**
whyNot.C: Oliver sign is a tracheal tug; his finding is **falling saturation on sitting up**
whyNot.D: Pemberton sign is facial flushing on raising the arms; his is **upright desaturation**

why: Platypnea-orthodeoxia is dyspnea and hypoxemia that worsen upright and improve lying flat. **Cirrhosis with upright desaturation** suggests hepatopulmonary syndrome with basal intrapulmonary shunting.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Lower ribs pull inward on inspiration
Dyspnea and hypoxia when upright, better lying
Trachea tugs downward with each heartbeat
Face flushes when both arms are raised
Substernal goiter obstructing the thoracic inlet

idea.rule: Dyspnea and desaturation when upright = hepatopulmonary syndrome or shunt.

set_title: Named triads I: Charcot triad, Reynolds pentad, Virchow triad, Whipple triad and Cushing triad
stem: A 52-year-old woman with known gallstones has 2 days of fever with rigors, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain. Blood pressure is 124/78 mm Hg and she is alert and oriented.
oneliner: 52F, gallstones + fever, rigors, jaundice, RUQ pain, BP 124/78 → ?

whyNot.A: Reynolds adds hypotension and confusion; she has **BP 124/78 and is alert**
whyNot.B: Virchow triad lists thrombosis risks; she has **fever, jaundice and RUQ pain**
whyNot.D: Whipple triad is hypoglycemia; hers is **fever, jaundice and RUQ pain**
whyNot.E: Cushing triad is hypertension, bradycardia, irregular breathing; her **BP is normal**

why: Fever, jaundice and **RUQ pain** are the Charcot triad of ascending cholangitis, here from a gallstone obstructing the bile duct.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Low glucose, symptoms, relief with glucose

idea.rule: Fever plus jaundice plus RUQ pain = ascending cholangitis.
also: Add hypotension and confusion for Reynolds pentad

set_title: Named triads I: Charcot triad, Reynolds pentad, Virchow triad, Whipple triad and Cushing triad
stem: A 68-year-old man with gallstones has 2 days of fever, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain. He is now confused and his blood pressure is 82/50 mm Hg.
oneliner: 68M, gallstones, fever, jaundice, RUQ pain + now confused, BP 82/50 → ?
ask: Which condition best explains this presentation?

whyNot.B: Cholecystitis rarely causes jaundice or shock; he has **jaundice, confusion and BP 82/50**
whyNot.C: Viral hepatitis lacks shock; he has **fever, RUQ pain and hypotension**
whyNot.D: Pancreatic cancer causes painless jaundice; he has **fever and RUQ pain**
whyNot.E: Encephalopathy lacks fever and RUQ pain; he has **hypotension with gallstones**

why: Charcot triad plus **confusion and hypotension** is Reynolds pentad, marking suppurative ascending cholangitis that needs urgent biliary drainage.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Low glucose, symptoms, relief with glucose

idea.rule: Fever, jaundice, RUQ pain, shock, confusion = suppurative cholangitis.
also: Treat with antibiotics and biliary decompression

set_title: Named triads II: Wernicke triad, Hakim triad, Plummer-Vinson triad, Meigs syndrome and Kartagener triad
stem: A 45-year-old woman has 1 year of difficulty swallowing solids, fatigue and spoon-shaped nails. Barium swallow shows a thin postcricoid web. Hemoglobin is 9.5 g/dL and MCV is 70 fL.
oneliner: 45F, dysphagia to solids, spoon nails + postcricoid web, microcytic anemia → ?
ask: Which cancer is she at increased risk for?

whyNot.A: Adenocarcinoma follows reflux and Barrett; she has an **upper web with anemia**
whyNot.C: Gastric cancer follows H pylori; her **upper web and dysphagia** are not gastric
whyNot.D: Liver cancer needs cirrhosis or hepatitis B; she has **dysphagia with a web**
whyNot.E: Her iron deficiency comes with a **web and dysphagia**, not a bowel lesion

why: Dysphagia, an upper esophageal web and **iron deficiency anemia** are the Plummer-Vinson triad, which raises the risk of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Dysphagia, esophageal webs, iron deficiency anemia
Iron deficiency; raises esophageal SCC risk
Ovarian fibroma, ascites, right pleural effusion

idea.rule: Dysphagia, esophageal web, iron deficiency = squamous cell cancer risk.
also: Treat with iron and web dilation

set_title: Abnormal movements: Asterixis, Cogwheel rigidity, Chorea, Hemiballismus, Intention tremor and Startle myoclonus
stem: A 58-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis is brought in with 2 days of confusion and day-night sleep reversal after a week of constipation. With arms outstretched and wrists dorsiflexed, both hands intermittently drop and then jerk back up about twice per second.
oneliner: 58M, cirrhosis, confusion, constipation + outstretched hands drop and jerk back up → ?

whyNot.B: Cogwheel is ratchet resistance to passive movement; his hands **drop while outstretched**
whyNot.C: Chorea is random flowing jerks; his are **regular lapses of held wrists**
whyNot.D: Hemiballismus is wild flinging of one limb; his are **small bilateral wrist lapses**
whyNot.E: Intention tremor appears nearing a target; his appears **with arms held still**

why: Brief loss of sustained muscle tone makes the held wrists flap. In **cirrhosis with confusion**, ammonia-driven encephalopathy is the cause; uremia and CO2 retention also produce it.

idea.rule: Flapping of outstretched wrists in a confused patient = asterixis, metabolic encephalopathy.

set_title: Appendicitis and abdominal wall signs: McBurney sign, Psoas sign, Obturator sign, Blumberg (rebound) sign and Carnett sign
stem: A 16-year-old boy has 18 hours of abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus and moved to the right lower abdomen, with nausea and temperature 38.6 C. Pressure one-third of the way from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus is most painful.
oneliner: 16-year-old boy, periumbilical pain moving right, fever + most pain one-third from ASIS to umbilicus → ?

whyNot.A: Psoas sign is pain on hip extension; his is **point tenderness on palpation**
whyNot.B: Obturator sign needs hip rotation; his is **point tenderness on palpation**
whyNot.C: Blumberg is pain on sudden release; his is **pain under steady pressure**
whyNot.E: Carnett is pain persisting with tensed muscles; his is **maximal tenderness at one point**

why: Pain one-third of the way from the right iliac spine to the umbilicus localizes the inflamed appendix to the parietal peritoneum. **Pain migrating from the umbilicus** is classic.

idea.rule: Pain one-third from right ASIS to umbilicus = McBurney sign, appendicitis.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Tenderness one-third from ASIS to umbilicus
Pain on passive right hip extension
Pain on internal rotation of flexed hip
Pain worse on sudden release of pressure
Pain persists or worsens with abdominal muscles tensed

set_title: Appendicitis and abdominal wall signs: McBurney sign, Psoas sign, Obturator sign, Blumberg (rebound) sign and Carnett sign
stem: A 24-year-old woman has 1 day of suprapubic pain, nausea and low-grade fever. Pregnancy test is negative. With her right hip and knee flexed, passive internal rotation of the hip increases her pain.
oneliner: 24F, suprapubic pain, nausea, low fever + pain on internal rotation of flexed right hip → ?

whyNot.B: McBurney is point tenderness on palpation; hers appears with **hip rotation**
whyNot.C: Psoas sign needs hip extension; hers is **internal rotation of the flexed hip**
whyNot.D: Blumberg is pain on release of pressure; hers is **internal hip rotation**
whyNot.E: Carnett needs tensed abdominal muscles; hers is **hip rotation**

why: Internal rotation stretches the obturator internus, which lies against an inflamed **pelvic appendix**. Suprapubic pain without urinary symptoms fits.

idea.rule: Pain on internal rotation of the flexed hip = obturator sign, pelvic appendix.
also: Obturator internus lies on pelvic wall

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Tenderness one-third from ASIS to umbilicus
Pain on passive right hip extension
Pain on internal rotation of flexed hip
Pain worse on sudden release of pressure
Pain persists or worsens with abdominal muscles tensed

set_title: Appendicitis and abdominal wall signs: McBurney sign, Psoas sign, Obturator sign, Blumberg (rebound) sign and Carnett sign
stem: A 22-year-old man has 1 day of dull right flank and lower abdominal pain, anorexia and low-grade fever. His pain worsens when he lies on his left side and the examiner extends his right hip (psoas sign). Urinalysis is normal and there is no costovertebral angle tenderness.
oneliner: 22M, right flank and lower pain, anorexia, fever + pain on right hip extension → appendix position?
ask: Which appendix location best explains this sign?

options.D: In front of the terminal ileum

whyNot.A: Pelvic appendix gives suprapubic pain; his pain **worsens with hip extension**
whyNot.C: A subhepatic appendix gives RUQ pain; his is **right flank and lower abdominal**
whyNot.D: An anterior appendix gives classic McBurney findings; his pain is **posterior with hip extension**
whyNot.E: That needs situs inversus; his pain is **right flank and lower abdomen**

why: A retrocecal appendix lies on the psoas muscle, so extending the hip stretches it and hurts. Pain may be **flank-predominant** with little peritoneal tenderness.

idea.rule: Pain on right hip extension = psoas sign, retrocecal appendix (or psoas abscess).
also: Psoas abscess gives the same sign

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Tenderness one-third from ASIS to umbilicus
Pain on passive right hip extension
Pain on internal rotation of flexed hip
Pain worse on sudden release of pressure
Pain persists or worsens with abdominal muscles tensed

set_title: Appendicitis and abdominal wall signs: McBurney sign, Psoas sign, Obturator sign, Blumberg (rebound) sign and Carnett sign
stem: A 38-year-old woman has 4 months of constant sharp left lower quadrant pain at a small spot, worse with sit-ups. Labs and CT are normal. Pain increases when she lifts her head and shoulders to tense the rectus muscles while the examiner presses on the tender spot (positive Carnett sign).
oneliner: 38F, 4 months of focal left lower quadrant pain, normal CT + pain worse with tensed rectus → source?
ask: Which source of pain best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Appendicitis has fever and progression over a day; hers is **chronic with normal CT**
whyNot.B: Cholecystitis causes RUQ pain with fever; hers is **chronic and left lower**
whyNot.D: Perforation gives board-like rigidity; hers is **months of focal pain, normal CT**
whyNot.E: Mesenteric ischemia causes pain after meals; hers is **worse with tensed muscles**

why: Tensing the abdominal wall guards visceral pain but increases pain from the wall itself. A **positive Carnett sign with normal imaging** suggests anterior cutaneous nerve entrapment or hernia.

idea.rule: Pain that worsens with tensed abdominal muscles = abdominal wall source.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Tenderness one-third from ASIS to umbilicus
Pain on passive right hip extension
Pain on internal rotation of flexed hip
Pain worse on sudden release of pressure
Pain persists or worsens with abdominal muscles tensed

set_title: Chronic liver disease signs: Caput medusae, Spider angiomas (spider nevi), Palmar erythema, Kayser-Fleischer rings and Terry nails
stem: A 54-year-old man with 20 years of heavy alcohol use has abdominal distension with shifting dullness. Dilated veins radiate outward from his umbilicus across the abdominal wall.
oneliner: 54M, 20 years heavy alcohol, ascites + dilated veins radiating from the umbilicus → ?

whyNot.A: Spider angiomas are small red skin lesions; his are **large veins around the umbilicus**
whyNot.B: Palmar erythema is on the palms; his finding is **veins around the umbilicus**
whyNot.C: Kayser-Fleischer rings are a corneal deposit; his finding is **on the abdominal wall**
whyNot.D: Terry nails are white nail beds; his finding is **veins around the umbilicus**

why: Portal hypertension reopens paraumbilical veins that carry portal blood to the abdominal wall veins. **Ascites** shows the portal hypertension.

idea.rule: Veins radiating from the umbilicus = caput medusae, portal hypertension.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Dilated veins radiating from the umbilicus
Central arteriole with radiating red legs
White nail beds, narrow pink distal band

set_title: Chronic liver disease signs: Caput medusae, Spider angiomas (spider nevi), Palmar erythema, Kayser-Fleischer rings and Terry nails
stem: A 56-year-old man with 25 years of alcohol use has gynecomastia and testicular atrophy. On his upper chest are several small red lesions, each with a central arteriole and thin radiating vessels that blanch when the center is pressed (spider angiomas).
oneliner: 56M, 25 years alcohol, gynecomastia + red lesions with radiating vessels → hormone?
ask: Which hormone best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Cortisol excess gives striae and central obesity; he has **gynecomastia and testicular atrophy**
whyNot.B: Aldosterone excess gives hypertension and low potassium; he has **gynecomastia**
whyNot.D: Testosterone excess would not cause **gynecomastia and testicular atrophy**
whyNot.E: Thyroxine excess gives tremor and weight loss; he has **gynecomastia with spider lesions**

why: The cirrhotic liver clears estrogen poorly, so vascular lesions, **gynecomastia and testicular atrophy** appear. Spider angiomas blanch on pressure to the center.

idea.rule: Spider angiomas, gynecomastia, palmar erythema = hyperestrogenism of cirrhosis.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Dilated veins radiating from the umbilicus
Central arteriole with radiating red legs
White nail beds, narrow pink distal band

set_title: Chronic liver disease signs: Caput medusae, Spider angiomas (spider nevi), Palmar erythema, Kayser-Fleischer rings and Terry nails
stem: A 52-year-old man who drinks 12 beers daily has red palms, most marked over the thenar and hypothenar eminences, that blanch with pressure. He also has gynecomastia, ascites and an albumin of 2.4 g/dL.
oneliner: 52M, 12 beers daily, ascites, albumin 2.4 + red thenar and hypothenar palms → ?
ask: Which condition best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Polycythemia causes facial plethora and itching; he has **ascites and albumin 2.4**
whyNot.C: Scleroderma causes tight skin and Raynaud; he has **ascites and low albumin**
whyNot.D: Rheumatoid arthritis causes joint disease; he has **ascites and albumin 2.4**
whyNot.E: Carbon monoxide gives cherry-red skin with headache; he has **ascites and low albumin**

why: Impaired estrogen clearance dilates palmar arterioles, reddening the thenar and hypothenar eminences. **Ascites and low albumin** show synthetic and portal failure.

idea.rule: Red thenar and hypothenar palms with ascites = cirrhosis (estrogen excess).

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Dilated veins radiating from the umbilicus
Central arteriole with radiating red legs
White nail beds, narrow pink distal band

set_title: Metastasis named signs: Virchow node, Sister Mary Joseph nodule, Krukenberg tumor of the ovary, Blumer shelf and Irish node
stem: A 64-year-old man has 3 months of early satiety and 7 kg weight loss. He has a firm, nontender 2-cm lymph node above the left clavicle.
oneliner: 64M, early satiety, weight loss + firm node above the left clavicle → ?

whyNot.B: Sister Mary Joseph is an umbilical nodule; his node is **above the left clavicle**
whyNot.C: Krukenberg is an ovarian mass; he is a man with **a supraclavicular node**
whyNot.D: Blumer shelf is a rectal finding; his is **a node above the clavicle**
whyNot.E: Irish node is in the left axilla; his node is **above the left clavicle**

why: Gastric cancer spreads through the thoracic duct to the left supraclavicular node. **Early satiety and weight loss** suggest the stomach primary.

idea.rule: Hard left supraclavicular node + abdominal cancer symptoms = Virchow node.
also: Thoracic duct drains to left venous angle

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Bilateral ovarian masses with signet ring cells
Hard rectal shelf felt on digital exam
Pelvic peritoneal metastases, e.g. gastric cancer

set_title: Metastasis named signs: Virchow node, Sister Mary Joseph nodule, Krukenberg tumor of the ovary, Blumer shelf and Irish node
stem: A 59-year-old woman has 4 months of abdominal swelling, early satiety and weight loss. Examination shows ascites and a firm 2-cm mass protruding from the umbilicus.
oneliner: 59F, abdominal swelling, early satiety, weight loss + firm umbilical mass → ?

whyNot.A: Virchow node is above the left clavicle; hers is **at the umbilicus**
whyNot.B: Krukenberg is an ovarian mass; hers **protrudes from the umbilicus**
whyNot.C: Blumer shelf is a rectal exam finding; hers is **an umbilical mass**
whyNot.D: Irish node is in the left axilla; hers is **at the umbilicus**

why: Intra-abdominal cancer, often gastric or ovarian, spreads along the round ligament remnant to the umbilicus. **Ascites with weight loss** points to advanced disease.

idea.rule: Firm umbilical mass + abdominal cancer symptoms = Sister Mary Joseph nodule.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Bilateral ovarian masses with signet ring cells
Hard rectal shelf felt on digital exam
Pelvic peritoneal metastases, e.g. gastric cancer

set_title: Metastasis named signs: Virchow node, Sister Mary Joseph nodule, Krukenberg tumor of the ovary, Blumer shelf and Irish node
stem: A 45-year-old woman has pelvic pain and early satiety. Imaging shows bilateral solid ovarian masses. Biopsy shows mucin-filled signet ring cells (Krukenberg tumor).
oneliner: 45F, pelvic pain, early satiety, bilateral ovarian masses with signet ring cells → primary?
ask: Where is the most likely primary tumor?

whyNot.A: Lung cancer rarely seeds both ovaries with mucin-filled signet cells; she has **early satiety**
whyNot.B: Pancreatic cancer gives painless jaundice; she has **early satiety and signet ring cells**
whyNot.C: Cervical cancer spreads locally with bleeding; she has **signet ring cells and early satiety**
whyNot.E: Hepatocellular carcinoma spreads to lung and bone; she has **bilateral ovarian signet ring masses**

why: Signet ring cells from a diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma seed both ovaries. **Early satiety** and mucin-filled signet cells point to the stomach.

idea.rule: Bilateral ovarian masses with signet ring cells = Krukenberg, usually gastric primary.
also: Colon and breast are less common

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Bilateral ovarian masses with signet ring cells
Hard rectal shelf felt on digital exam
Pelvic peritoneal metastases, e.g. gastric cancer

set_title: Metastasis named signs: Virchow node, Sister Mary Joseph nodule, Krukenberg tumor of the ovary, Blumer shelf and Irish node
stem: A 66-year-old man with gastric adenocarcinoma has pelvic fullness and constipation. On digital rectal examination a hard, nodular, shelf-like mass is felt anterior to the rectum (Blumer shelf). The rectal mucosa is normal.
oneliner: 66M, known gastric cancer, pelvic fullness + hard shelf on rectal exam, normal mucosa → ?

options.B: Primary rectal adenocarcinoma invading the wall

whyNot.B: Rectal cancer arises in the mucosa; his **rectal mucosa is normal**
whyNot.C: BPH gives a smooth, symmetric prostate; his mass is **hard, nodular and shelf-like**
whyNot.D: Internal hemorrhoids are not palpable normally; his is **a hard shelf**
whyNot.E: Impaction is soft stool; his is **a fixed shelf under normal mucosa**

why: Tumor cells drop into the rectovesical or rectouterine pouch and form a hard shelf felt through the rectum. It shows **peritoneal metastasis** from the gastric cancer.

idea.rule: Hard shelf in front of the rectum with normal mucosa = pelvic peritoneal metastasis.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Bilateral ovarian masses with signet ring cells
Hard rectal shelf felt on digital exam
Pelvic peritoneal metastases, e.g. gastric cancer

set_title: GI imaging signs I: Bird's beak sign, Corkscrew esophagus, Double bubble sign, Apple core lesion, Lead pipe colon and String sign
stem: A 36-year-old woman has 8 months of difficulty swallowing both solids and liquids, regurgitation of undigested food and 5 kg weight loss. A barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus tapering smoothly to a point at the gastroesophageal junction.
oneliner: 36F, dysphagia to solids and liquids, regurgitation + dilated esophagus tapering at the GE junction → ?

whyNot.A: Corkscrew shows spiral contractions; hers is **a dilated esophagus tapering to a point**
whyNot.B: Double bubble is a newborn air pattern; hers is **a tapered esophagus on barium**
whyNot.D: Apple core is annular colon narrowing; hers is **a tapered esophagus**
whyNot.E: String sign is a thin ileal barium thread; hers is **a tapered esophagus**

why: Loss of myenteric inhibitory neurons leaves the lower esophageal sphincter unable to relax, so the esophagus dilates above a **smooth tapered narrowing**.

idea.rule: Dilated esophagus tapering to the LES = bird's beak, achalasia.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Two air-filled bubbles, no distal gas
Thin barium line in terminal ileum

set_title: GI imaging signs I: Bird's beak sign, Corkscrew esophagus, Double bubble sign, Apple core lesion, Lead pipe colon and String sign
stem: A 6-hour-old newborn with upslanting palpebral fissures and a single palmar crease vomits green fluid after the first feed. An abdominal radiograph shows two air-filled structures in the upper abdomen and no gas below.
oneliner: 6-hour-old newborn, Down features, bilious vomiting + two air-filled upper structures, no distal gas → ?

whyNot.A: Bird's beak is a dilated esophagus; his film shows **two upper air bubbles**
whyNot.C: Corkscrew is spiral esophageal contractions; his film shows **two air-filled structures**
whyNot.D: Apple core is annular colon narrowing; his film shows **two upper air bubbles**
whyNot.E: String sign is an ileal barium thread; his film shows **two upper air bubbles**

why: Air fills the stomach and proximal duodenum above the obstruction, with **no gas distally**. Down syndrome predisposes to duodenal atresia.

idea.rule: Two gas bubbles and no distal gas in a newborn = double bubble, duodenal atresia.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Two air-filled bubbles, no distal gas
Thin barium line in terminal ileum

set_title: GI imaging signs I: Bird's beak sign, Corkscrew esophagus, Double bubble sign, Apple core lesion, Lead pipe colon and String sign
stem: A 66-year-old man has 3 months of fatigue and a change in bowel habit. Hemoglobin is 9.0 g/dL with MCV 72 fL and low ferritin. Barium enema shows a short circumferential sigmoid narrowing with sharply overhanging edges (apple core lesion).
oneliner: 66M, fatigue, iron-deficiency anemia + short sigmoid narrowing with overhanging edges → ?
ask: Which condition best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Ulcerative colitis gives a smooth, tubular colon; his is **a short focal annular narrowing**
whyNot.B: Crohn narrows the ileum; his is **a single sigmoid narrowing**
whyNot.C: Diverticulitis gives left lower pain and fever; he has **iron-deficiency anemia**
whyNot.D: Ischemic colitis follows hypoperfusion with thumbprinting; he has **chronic iron-deficiency anemia**

why: A circumferential adenocarcinoma narrows the lumen with overhanging edges. **Iron-deficiency anemia in an older man** indicates occult colonic bleeding.

idea.rule: Iron-deficiency anemia in an older adult + apple core lesion = colorectal cancer.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Two air-filled bubbles, no distal gas
Thin barium line in terminal ileum

set_title: GI imaging signs I: Bird's beak sign, Corkscrew esophagus, Double bubble sign, Apple core lesion, Lead pipe colon and String sign
stem: A 22-year-old man has 8 months of crampy right lower abdominal pain, diarrhea and a perianal fistula. A small bowel follow-through shows a long narrow stretch of terminal ileum with a thin thread of barium (string sign).
oneliner: 22M, crampy right lower pain, diarrhea, perianal fistula + thin barium thread in terminal ileum → ?
ask: Which condition best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Ulcerative colitis spares the small bowel and fistulas; his **terminal ileum is narrowed**
whyNot.B: Celiac affects the proximal bowel; his is **terminal ileum with a fistula**
whyNot.C: Ischemic colitis is sudden in older patients; he has **months of ileal stricture**
whyNot.E: Giardiasis causes foul diarrhea without stricture or fistula; he has **a perianal fistula**

why: Transmural inflammation and fibrosis narrow the terminal ileum to a thread. **Perianal fistula** and ileal involvement point to Crohn disease.

idea.rule: Terminal ileum narrowed to a thread + fistula = Crohn disease.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Two air-filled bubbles, no distal gas
Thin barium line in terminal ileum

set_title: GI imaging signs II: Thumbprinting, Coffee bean sign, Target sign, Rigler sign and Colon cutoff sign
stem: An 82-year-old nursing-home resident has 2 days of abdominal distension, constipation and no flatus. The abdomen is tympanic. A radiograph shows a massively dilated, inverted U-shaped gas loop rising from the pelvis to the right upper quadrant.
oneliner: 82M, nursing home, 2 days distension, no flatus + inverted U gas loop from the pelvis → ?

whyNot.A: Thumbprinting is thickened, indented bowel wall; his film shows **a giant inverted-U loop**
whyNot.C: Target sign is ultrasound rings; his is **a giant gas loop on radiograph**
whyNot.D: Rigler needs free air outlining the wall; his is **a giant inverted-U loop**
whyNot.E: Colon cutoff ends at the splenic flexure; his is **a pelvic loop**

why: A twisted sigmoid forms a closed loop that balloons into an inverted U with a central cleft. **Elderly, constipated and institutionalized** are the classic risks.

idea.rule: Giant inverted-U gas loop from the pelvis = coffee bean, sigmoid volvulus.
also: Cecal volvulus: bean toward left upper quadrant

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Thick bowel wall indentations on x-ray
Both sides of bowel wall visible
Gas stops abruptly at splenic flexure

set_title: GI imaging signs II: Thumbprinting, Coffee bean sign, Target sign, Rigler sign and Colon cutoff sign
stem: A 14-month-old boy has episodes of screaming with drawing up of his legs, vomiting and a currant-jelly stool. A sausage-shaped mass is palpable in the right upper abdomen. Ultrasound shows concentric alternating bright and dark rings.
oneliner: 14-month-old boy, colicky screaming, vomiting, currant-jelly stool + concentric rings on ultrasound → ?

whyNot.A: Thumbprinting is indented bowel wall on radiograph; his ultrasound shows **concentric rings**
whyNot.B: Coffee bean is a giant gas loop on radiograph; his ultrasound shows **concentric rings**
whyNot.D: Rigler is free air outlining the bowel wall; his ultrasound shows **concentric rings**
whyNot.E: Colon cutoff is gas ending at the splenic flexure; his ultrasound shows **concentric rings**

why: The telescoped bowel segment layers into concentric rings on cross-section ultrasound. **Colicky pain and currant-jelly stool** in a toddler indicate intussusception.

idea.rule: Concentric rings on ultrasound in a colicky toddler = target sign, intussusception.
also: Lead point: Meckel or Peyer patches

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Thick bowel wall indentations on x-ray
Both sides of bowel wall visible
Gas stops abruptly at splenic flexure

set_title: GI imaging signs II: Thumbprinting, Coffee bean sign, Target sign, Rigler sign and Colon cutoff sign
stem: A 78-year-old woman has sudden left lower abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea one day after a prolonged hypotensive episode during cardiac surgery. A radiograph shows thickened colonic wall with regular blunt indentations (thumbprinting).
oneliner: 78F, bloody diarrhea a day after surgical hypotension + thumbprinting → ?
ask: Which condition best explains this sign?

whyNot.B: Ulcerative colitis builds over weeks; hers followed **a hypotensive episode**
whyNot.C: Diverticulitis causes fever and localized pain, not **bloody diarrhea after hypotension**
whyNot.D: Volvulus shows a giant gas loop; hers shows **thickened indented colon wall**
whyNot.E: Cancer causes a fixed narrowing over months; hers is **acute after hypotension**

why: Submucosal edema and hemorrhage from poor perfusion thicken the colonic wall into thumbprints. **Hypotension in an older patient** is the classic setup.

idea.rule: Thumbprinting + bloody diarrhea after hypoperfusion = ischemic colitis.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Thick bowel wall indentations on x-ray
Both sides of bowel wall visible
Gas stops abruptly at splenic flexure

set_title: GI imaging signs II: Thumbprinting, Coffee bean sign, Target sign, Rigler sign and Colon cutoff sign
stem: A 45-year-old man who drinks heavily has 2 days of severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and vomiting. Lipase is 15 times normal. A radiograph shows a gas-filled transverse colon ending abruptly at the splenic flexure (colon cutoff sign).
oneliner: 45M, heavy drinking, epigastric pain to the back, lipase 15x + gas stops at splenic flexure → ?
ask: Which condition best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Volvulus shows a giant gas loop; his gas **stops at the splenic flexure**
whyNot.B: Perforation shows free air; his picture is **lipase 15 times normal**
whyNot.C: Cholecystitis gives RUQ pain; his is **epigastric to the back with lipase 15x**
whyNot.D: Toxic megacolon dilates the whole colon; his pain is **epigastric with lipase 15x**

why: Inflammation spreads from the pancreas along the phrenicocolic ligament, spasming the colon at the splenic flexure. **Lipase 15x normal** confirms pancreatitis.

idea.rule: Gas stopping at the splenic flexure + epigastric pain = acute pancreatitis.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Thick bowel wall indentations on x-ray
Both sides of bowel wall visible
Gas stops abruptly at splenic flexure

set_title: Pediatric abdominal signs: Olive sign, Currant jelly stool, Dance sign, Squirt sign and Double bubble sign
stem: A 4-week-old firstborn boy has had 10 days of forceful nonbilious vomiting after every feed, and he is hungry again right after. He is dehydrated and has lost weight. During a feed, a firm, mobile, 2-cm mass is palpable in the epigastrium. Serum chloride is low and bicarbonate is high.
oneliner: 4-week-old boy, projectile nonbilious vomiting + firm epigastric mass → ?

whyNot.A: Currant jelly stool is bloody mucus stool; he has **no bloody stool**
whyNot.C: Dance sign is an empty right lower quadrant; his mass is **epigastric**
whyNot.D: Squirt sign follows a rectal exam; he has **projectile vomiting and a palpable mass**
whyNot.E: Double bubble is a bilious-vomiting X-ray sign; he has **a palpable epigastric mass**

why: A firm epigastric mass felt in an infant with projectile vomiting is the olive sign: the hypertrophied pylorus. **Hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis** supports it.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Empty right lower quadrant on palpation
Two gas bubbles, no distal bowel gas

idea.rule: Projectile nonbilious vomiting + epigastric mass = olive sign = pyloric stenosis.

set_title: Pediatric abdominal signs: Olive sign, Currant jelly stool, Dance sign, Squirt sign and Double bubble sign
stem: A 14-month-old boy has had 6 hours of episodic screaming with his legs drawn up, separated by quiet, lethargic periods. He vomited twice. He then passes dark red blood mixed with mucus per rectum. A sausage-shaped mass is palpable in the right upper abdomen.
oneliner: 14-month-old boy, colicky pain + passing dark blood and mucus → ?

whyNot.A: Olive sign is an epigastric mass with projectile vomiting; he passes **bloody mucus stool**
whyNot.B: Dance sign is a palpation finding; he passes **blood and mucus per rectum**
whyNot.C: Squirt sign is explosive stool after rectal exam; he passes **dark blood and mucus**
whyNot.D: Double bubble is a neonatal X-ray sign; he is **14 months old**

why: Stool mixed with blood and mucus is currant jelly stool, from mucosal ischemia as the telescoped bowel loses its blood supply. **Colicky pain with a sausage mass** fits intussusception.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Empty right lower quadrant on palpation
Two gas bubbles, no distal bowel gas

idea.rule: Colicky pain + bloody mucus stool in a toddler = currant jelly stool = intussusception.
also: Ileocolic is the most common site

set_title: Pediatric abdominal signs: Olive sign, Currant jelly stool, Dance sign, Squirt sign and Double bubble sign
stem: A 9-month-old boy has had two episodes of colicky crying with his legs drawn up over 12 hours, with a lethargic interval between them. Palpation of the right lower quadrant feels empty (Dance sign), and a sausage-shaped mass is felt in the right upper quadrant.
oneliner: 9-month-old boy, colicky pain + empty right lower quadrant → ?
ask: Which condition best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Pyloric stenosis presents at 4 weeks with vomiting; he is **9 months old**
whyNot.B: Hirschsprung presents with delayed meconium; he has **colicky pain with a sausage mass**
whyNot.D: Appendicitis gives steady pain and fever; his pain is **colicky with lethargy between episodes**
whyNot.E: Volvulus causes bilious vomiting; he has **intermittent pain with a sausage-shaped mass**

why: An empty right lower quadrant means the cecum has been pulled away by telescoping bowel (Dance sign). With a **sausage mass and colicky pain**, this is intussusception.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Empty right lower quadrant on palpation
Two gas bubbles, no distal bowel gas

idea.rule: Empty right lower quadrant + colicky pain in an infant = Dance sign = intussusception.
also: Lead point may be a Meckel diverticulum
Peyer patch hypertrophy after viral illness

set_title: Pediatric abdominal signs: Olive sign, Currant jelly stool, Dance sign, Squirt sign and Double bubble sign
stem: A 2-day-old full-term boy has not passed meconium and has a distended abdomen with bilious vomiting. After a digital rectal exam, a forceful gush of foul stool and gas is expelled (Squirt sign). Contrast enema shows a narrow rectum and a dilated proximal colon.
oneliner: 2-day-old boy, no meconium + explosive stool after rectal exam → cells?
ask: Absence of which cells best explains this sign?

whyNot.B: Cajal cell loss gives dysmotility, not a **narrow distal segment with proximal dilation**
whyNot.C: Enterochromaffin cells secrete serotonin and do not control **distal colonic relaxation**
whyNot.D: Goblet cell loss reduces mucus, not causing **a narrow rectum**
whyNot.E: Paneth cells secrete antimicrobials in the small bowel; **the rectum is the problem**

why: Explosive stool after rectal exam is the squirt sign of Hirschsprung disease: the aganglionic segment stays contracted, so the exam releases proximal stool. **Narrow rectum, dilated colon** confirm it.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Empty right lower quadrant on palpation
Two gas bubbles, no distal bowel gas

idea.rule: Delayed meconium + explosive stool after rectal exam = Hirschsprung = no ganglion cells.
also: RET mutations; association with Down syndrome

set_title: Skin signs of internal disease: Trousseau sign of malignancy, Leser-Trelat sign, Acanthosis nigricans, Necrolytic migratory erythema and Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
stem: A 68-year-old man has lost 7 kg in 3 months. Over 6 weeks, more than 40 itchy, waxy, brown, stuck-on plaques have erupted on his back and chest. Stool is guaiac positive.
oneliner: 68M, weight loss + guaiac-positive stool + sudden crop of waxy stuck-on plaques → ?

whyNot.B: Trousseau sign is migratory venous thrombosis; he has **stuck-on brown plaques**
whyNot.C: Acanthosis nigricans is velvety flexural hyperpigmentation; his lesions are **waxy, stuck-on plaques**
whyNot.D: Necrolytic migratory erythema is a spreading blistering rash, not **waxy stuck-on plaques**
whyNot.E: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy causes clubbing and bone pain, not **waxy plaques**

why: A **sudden eruption of 40 stuck-on plaques** (seborrheic keratoses) with weight loss is the Leser-Trelat sign, a paraneoplastic marker, classically of GI adenocarcinoma.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Sudden eruption of many seborrheic keratoses
Velvety dark plaques in neck, axillae
Insulin resistance; abrupt onset: gastric adenocarcinoma
Spreading red blistering rash, groin, face
Clubbing with painful periostitis of long bones

idea.rule: Sudden crop of seborrheic keratoses + weight loss = Leser-Trelat; seek GI adenocarcinoma.
also: Rapid rise in number or size

set_title: Abdominal signs: Murphy, Rovsing, Cullen, Grey Turner, Courvoisier and Kehr
stem: A 42-year-old woman has had 10 hours of constant right upper quadrant pain that began after a fatty meal. Temperature is 38.4°C. The examiner presses below the right costal margin and asks her to breathe in deeply; she stops mid-breath because of sharp pain.
oneliner: 42F, RUQ pain after a fatty meal, fever + stops mid-breath on right subcostal pressure → ?

whyNot.A: Rovsing sign is RLQ pain on LLQ pressure; her pain is **right upper quadrant**
whyNot.B: Cullen sign is periumbilical bruising; her finding is **stopping mid-breath** from pain
whyNot.D: Courvoisier sign is painless jaundice; she has **sharp pain and fever**
whyNot.E: Kehr sign is left shoulder pain; her pain is **below the right costal margin**

why: Stopping inspiration from pain during right subcostal pressure is Murphy sign. The descending inflamed gallbladder meets the examiner's fingers.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Pain stops inspiration during RUQ palpation
Painless jaundice with palpable, nontender gallbladder

idea.rule: RUQ pain + fever + inspiratory arrest on palpation = acute cholecystitis.

set_title: Abdominal signs: Murphy, Rovsing, Cullen, Grey Turner, Courvoisier and Kehr
stem: A 17-year-old boy has pain that began around the umbilicus yesterday and has moved to the right lower quadrant. He has no appetite and a temperature of 38.1°C. He is most tender at McBurney point. Deep pressure on the left lower quadrant causes pain in the right lower quadrant.
oneliner: 17M, periumbilical pain moving to RLQ, fever + LLQ pressure hurts the RLQ → ?
ask: Which sign does the last finding describe?

whyNot.B: Murphy sign is inspiratory arrest on RUQ palpation; his pain is **right lower quadrant**
whyNot.C: Grey Turner sign is flank bruising; he has **pain on left-sided pressure**
whyNot.D: Courvoisier sign is painless jaundice, palpable gallbladder; he has **fever and RLQ pain**
whyNot.E: Kehr sign is referred left shoulder pain; his pain is **felt in the right lower quadrant**

why: Left-sided pressure pushes gas and fluid toward the inflamed appendix, causing right-sided pain. McBurney point lies one-third of the way from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Pain stops inspiration during RUQ palpation
Painless jaundice with palpable, nontender gallbladder

idea.rule: Periumbilical pain moving to the RLQ + Rovsing sign = acute appendicitis.
also: Psoas and obturator signs suggest atypical positions
Lumen blocked by fecalith or lymphoid hyperplasia

set_title: Abdominal signs: Murphy, Rovsing, Cullen, Grey Turner, Courvoisier and Kehr
stem: A 50-year-old man who drinks heavily has had 3 days of severe epigastric pain radiating to the back. Serum lipase is 12 times normal. On day 3 he has bluish bruising of both flanks (Grey Turner sign).
oneliner: 50M, heavy drinking, epigastric pain to the back, lipase 12x + Grey Turner sign → mechanism?
ask: Which mechanism best explains this sign?

options.A: Blood tracking along the falciform ligament
options.B: Vitamin K malabsorption from fat loss

whyNot.A: That gives periumbilical Cullen sign; his bruising is **on both flanks**
whyNot.B: Malabsorption takes months; his bruising appeared **3 days into acute pain**
whyNot.C: Thrombocytopenia bruises diffusely; his bruising is **limited to both flanks**
whyNot.E: Bilirubin stains skin yellow; his flanks are **bluish**

why: Hemorrhagic pancreatitis bleeds into the retroperitoneum, and the blood tracks out to the flanks. It appears a day or more in and marks severe disease.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Pain stops inspiration during RUQ palpation
Painless jaundice with palpable, nontender gallbladder

idea.rule: Flank (Grey Turner) or periumbilical (Cullen) bruising = retroperitoneal bleeding, often severe pancreatitis.

set_title: Abdominal signs: Murphy, Rovsing, Cullen, Grey Turner, Courvoisier and Kehr
stem: A 68-year-old man who smokes has lost 8 kg over 3 months and has dark urine and pale stools. He has no abdominal pain. He is jaundiced, and a smooth, nontender gallbladder is palpable below the right costal margin (Courvoisier sign).
oneliner: 68M, smoker, weight loss, painless jaundice + palpable nontender gallbladder → ?
ask: Which condition best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Stones cause painful jaundice and a scarred gallbladder; his jaundice is **painless**
whyNot.C: Cholecystitis causes fever and RUQ pain; he has **no abdominal pain**
whyNot.D: PBC does not distend the gallbladder; his is **smooth and palpable**
whyNot.E: Hepatitis A is a short febrile illness; he has **lost 8 kg over 3 months**

why: A tumor slowly blocks the distal bile duct, so a healthy gallbladder distends without pain. Gallstone disease scars the gallbladder, so it rarely enlarges.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Pain stops inspiration during RUQ palpation
Painless jaundice with palpable, nontender gallbladder

idea.rule: Painless jaundice + palpable nontender gallbladder + weight loss = pancreatic head cancer.
